RC10.3 repairs documentation gates that treated saved source snapshots and raw review output as
newly authored guidance. Within `docs/**/evidence/**`, raw Markdown is an artifact; authored
`README.md` and `index.md` summaries remain checked. Evidence `before/` and `after/` subtrees
retain their original metadata and relative links. Their copies no longer create false missing-link
or duplicate-document failures.

The enabled developer catalog's index, references and guides remain live documentation even in
evidence directories. Catalog sources can reference raw artifacts, but their existence and local
paths remain checked. Active execution plans retain all existing requirements. Real broken live
guides, unsafe local links, duplicate authored IDs and invalid catalogs still block.

The common lifecycle now accepts proposal, accepted, working, provisional, in-progress and research
alongside the existing names. Lessons and active plans keep their narrower rules. Lifecycle labels
do not grant approval or execution authority. Unknown labels report the accepted vocabulary.
Portable authoring guidance explains where to save raw evidence and how to summarize it.

The installed greenfield release suite now proves successful evidence retention, a failing broken
live guide, repair through the normal shipped check command, and unchanged frozen-copy bytes.
Existing fixture-based context and fallback proof remains required. This deterministic correction
does not establish live provider benefits or token savings.

No profile schema change or snapshot rewrite is required. Upgrade deliberately at a pause seam.
Absolute cross-repository filesystem citations, missing live targets and incomplete authored
metadata remain separate findings. This release does not update adopter checkouts automatically.
